title: Bellarmine: images of Christ and the Saints venerated per se and properly, not only as stand-ins
source_text: XLIV. Ita quoque sentit Bellarminus cujus haec est propositio, Imagines Christi & Sanctorum venerandae sunt, non solum per accidens, vel improprie, sed etiam per se et proprie, ita ut ipsae terminent venerationem ut in se considerantur, & non solum ut vicem gerunt exemplaris. De Ecclesia triumphante libro secundo capite vigesimo primo.
pass_a_gloss: So also Bellarmine thinks, whose proposition is this: The Images of Christ and of the Saints are to be venerated, not only per accidents or improperly, but also per se and properly, so that they themselves terminate the veneration as they are considered in themselves, and not only as they bear the place of the exemplar. On the Triumphant Church, book two, chapter twenty-one.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's proposition: images of Christ and the Saints are venerated per se and properly.
They terminate veneration as considered in themselves—not only as stand-ins for the exemplar (De Ecclesia triumphante II.21).

lemmas.gloss: they bear the place of the exemplar

choices.why: Images as terminus, not mere occasions.
